clue.text: Money-hoarder's endless wretchedness

indicators.note: endless says the word for wretchedness loses its final letter

parts.note: wretchedness is misery

explanation.surface: A grasping skinflint is condemned to unending unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the Y from MISERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who hoards money and spends as little as possible is the classic skinflint.

clue.text: Drug satisfied a politician and governor in the main resort

parts.note: met as in met a demand

indicators.note: in places the politician group inside the shuffled phrase
resort is read as re-sort, sort again

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
HE, His Excellency, the title of a governor

explanation.surface: A narcotic pleased a politician and a governor at a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort, an anagram signal, not a holiday spot; the anagram of 'the main' is split by the inserted group after its first letter. A governor is styled His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Methamphetamine is a powerful stimulant narcotic, often called crystal meth.

clue.text: Nagging woman flogged outside clubs

indicators.note: outside says the word for flogged wraps around the card suit letter

parts.note: to flog something is slang for selling it
C is short for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A shrew is beaten outside some nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogged' means sold, not whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A scold is an old term for a woman who habitually finds fault and rails at others.

clue.text: Bring up second reminder for a saver

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the pieces replace the letter A

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
a cue is a prompt

explanation.surface: Raising another prompt about a savings account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts S CUE in place of the A in REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saves another from danger is a lifesaver or deliverer.

clue.text: Wakeful type in county recalled famous murderer

parts.note: Som is the standard abbreviation for Somerset, an English county

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the murderer's name is written backwards

parts.note: Cain, who killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot sleep in a rural county is haunted by a notorious killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns CAIN into NIAC. SOM is Somerset, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually lies awake, unable to sleep, is a wakeful sort of person.

clue.text: Spiritual leader, one with mother in Newcastle, perhaps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mam is the northern English and Geordie word for mother

explanation.surface: A religious figure living with his mum in the North East.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle, in north-east England, is one place where 'mam' is said for mum.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and is a Muslim religious figure.

clue.text: Something fishy originally marking a jolly prim teacher

parts.note: a school is a group of fish

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of marking

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A strait-laced teacher grades work while smelling something suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is an old naval nickname for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmarm is a strict, old-fashioned female teacher, so a prim one.

clue.text: Generator of glossy, potentially clear source of ointment

parts.note: a glossy is one kind of magazine, a mag
net means clear after deductions, as in profit

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of ointment

explanation.surface: Something makes a shiny lotion, possibly a clear one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glossy' is a noun here, a glossy magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A magneto is a small electrical generator using permanent magnets, as in engine ignition.

clue.text: Sibling's declaration soldier left inside entrance to officers' mess?

parts.note: a brother might declare 'I'm bro'

indicators.note: inside places the letter for left within the soldier

parts.note: GI, an American soldier

indicators.note: entrance to picks the first letter of officers'

explanation.surface: A brother's statement in the officers' dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the military dining room the surface implies; it is the definition, a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, embarrassing situation, a tangle, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Top men on a course oddly existing at the same time

indicators.note: oddly signals the letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: The leading golfers play strangely in the same round.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporaneous things happen or exist in the same period.

clue.text: Old Chinese philosophy briefly followed by every European leader

indicators.note: briefly signals the philosophy's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Taoism, the teaching of Lao Tzu
every means each

explanation.surface: An ancient Eastern philosophy is quickly adopted by every leader in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the M of TAOISM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish prime minister holds this title, making that office-holder a head of government in Europe.

clue.text: State of small number knocked back by speaker's gift

parts.note: the gift of the gab is a talent for fluent speech

indicators.note: knocked back is read as turned backwards, so the abbreviation is written in reverse

parts.note: No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A modest figure is rebuffed by a fine orator's talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' signals the reversal; 'by' just means next to, placing it after the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a country in west-central Africa, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Enthusiasm is more exhausting, as Cockneys may say

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial H, so the comparative is pronounced as a Londoner would

parts.note: something more exhausting is harder work

explanation.surface: Keenness is said to be more tiring, in East London speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their H's, so HARDER comes out as 'arder, matching the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate eagerness, a close synonym for keen enthusiasm.

clue.text: Its occupants may be collared pinching grain

definitions.text: Its occupants may be collared pinching grain

parts.words: Its occupants may be collared pinching grain
parts.note: the occupants are collared doves, birds named for a neck marking, who might be pecking up grain rather than being arrested for stealing it

explanation.surface: The residents might be arrested for stealing corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collared' and 'pinching' suggest a police arrest for theft; really they describe collared doves and their pecking at grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure for housing pigeons and similar birds is home to collared doves among others.

clue.text: Give away ring? One might expect to sell it

definitions.text: One might expect to sell it

parts.note: to shop someone is to inform on them
a keeper is a ring worn to hold a wedding ring in place

explanation.surface: Should you part with a ring? A buyer would expect to resell it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the ring: a trader expects to sell such stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a person who sells goods, so expects to sell what is brought in.

clue.text: Fabric man or woman keeps in hotel safe at front

indicators.note: at front places the safe's slang word ahead of the rest

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: keeps in says the unisex name holds the hotel letter inside it

parts.note: Sam can be a man's or a woman's name
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone stores cloth in a hotel safe, at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps in' signals the containment. 'Safe' is a noun, not an adjective: peter is old thieves' slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a thick corded ribbon or heavy woollen cloth, a type of textile.

clue.text: Shocking start for uncle in vehicle — Greek, reportedly

indicators.note: in places the uncle's first letter within the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle on rails

indicators.note: start for picks the first letter of uncle
reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, so Greek

explanation.surface: An uncle gets a jolt riding a tram, a Greek one, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the containment; 'reportedly' signals a sound-alike, since Attic (of Athens) is spelt with two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: Traumatic events are deeply distressing, causing shock.

clue.text: Blooming supplier of meat and sauce

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a flowering plant, so it stands loosely for the noun

parts.note: an ox provides beef
sauce and lip both mean cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A source of beef and gravy for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' means impudence here, not gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a flowering plant of the primrose family, something that blooms.

clue.text: Send Irishman over with key

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: over signals the Irish name is turned around

parts.note: Liam is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: A man from Ireland is sent across with a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LIAM into MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a message electronically is to dispatch it, the verb sense of sending.

clue.text: More recent article identifying old Roman palace

parts.note: later means more recent
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newer piece of writing pinpoints an ancient palace in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran Palace in Rome was the papal residence for centuries.

clue.text: Culturally pretentious turn digested by a reveller

indicators.note: digested by means taken inside, so the word for 'a' swallows the others

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
arty means affectedly artistic
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: A pseudo-intellectual's turn is endured by someone having a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digested by' signals the containment; 'a' is read as 'per', as in a price a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends celebrations and enjoys them noisily is a merrymaker.

clue.text: Get kicks with zany foreign banker

definitions.note: a river abroad, a banker being a thing with banks

indicators.note: kicks suggests the letters are booted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A foreign financier gets thrills from wild behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a river, something with banks, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest river, so a waterway abroad with banks.

clue.text: Acknowledged being enrolled as member

definitions.meaning: conceded or confessed something to be true
allowed entry to a society or club

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having joined an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitting is both conceding a truth and allowing someone into a body as a member.

clue.text: Educational establishment's working agreement

parts.note: uni is short for university, here with the possessive 's
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: A college's practical arrangement is in operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting in harmony, so the word stands for accord.

clue.text: Quiet son taking a couple of horses across America

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the horse letters straddle the country's abbreviation

parts.note: H is slang for horse, heroin; two of them is HH
US

explanation.surface: A boy is hushed while carrying two horses over the American border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts US between the two H's.
explanation.definitionFit: Shush is a command to be silent, so it stands for the imperative quiet.

clue.text: Fellow caught with intoxicating liquor

parts.note: ale is beer
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A man is caught with strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a man's first name, so it stands for a chap or bloke.

clue.text: Bury doctor in US abandoning Washington finally

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor in America

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Washington

explanation.surface: An American doctor buries someone after leaving the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops N, the last letter of Washington, from INTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to lay a body in a grave, a formal synonym for burial.

clue.text: Hanger-on in largely civilised old Communist executive

indicators.note: in places the clinging seed inside the rest
largely means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: civilised means polite
a bur is a seed head that sticks to clothing

explanation.surface: A parasite in a mostly refined, old-fashioned setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last letter of the word for civilised; 'in' puts the clinging seed head inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of the Soviet Communist Party.

clue.text: Bizarre device for converting motion

definitions.meaning: an off-centre wheel or disc that turns rotation into back-and-forth movement

explanation.surface: A strange gadget for changing how things move.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means oddball and also names an off-centre engineering cam.

clue.text: Spirit revealed albeit briefly in French art

indicators.note: in places the shortened conjunction within the French verb

parts.note: es is French for 'art' as in 'thou art', from the verb to be
tho is the short spelling of though, meaning albeit

explanation.surface: A spirit is glimpsed, if only briefly, in French painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the archaic verb (thou art), French ES, not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit of a culture or group is its guiding character.
